one_line_contribution: A crossover identification device for container substitution: holding the optimized instruction and the test instances fixed, compare the gain of the memory bank distilled from the same training episodes that instruction was optimized on (cells 6, 10) against the gain of a bank distilled from a disjoint half (cells 7, 9), so that the resulting Delta_info is attributable to shared episode provenance rather than to headroom, level, or token budget.
closest_prior_work: Three, in descending threat. (1) EvoAgentBench (2607.05202) already puts ReasoningBank, Memento and GEPA on identical 528/267 trajectories with Qwen3.5-27B as a backbone; the proposal honestly concedes this and withdraws its v2 novelty sentence. What survives is the combined cell and the crossover, which EvoAgentBench genuinely lacks — but this narrows the contribution from 'first three-way comparison' to 'a provenance contrast added to an existing table.' (2) MIPROv2 (2406.11695) is the framing precedent a reviewer names first: instruction-only vs demonstration-only vs joint on one training set is the two-container ablation, and its recurring finding that the split is task-dependent already predicts the proposal's likely 'mixed/complementarity' outcome. The retrieval read and the held-out-episode crossover are the real deltas. (3) Experience Distillation (2607.21051) measures the identical estimand shape — what fraction of an in-context gain survives when the information is moved to a second container — with weights rather than an instruction as the container. Together these leave the proposal with a real but incremental methodological delta rather than a new question.
strongest_objection: The confirmatory endpoint may be structurally powerless in the chosen environment, and a null would be uninterpretable. Delta_info requires that B_a contain content that is useful on S_test AND specific to half a. But S_train_a and S_train_b are 400-episode halves drawn by seeded stratified random split (50/30/20 by dataset) from pooled HotpotQA/MuSiQue/2Wiki, so the two halves are exchangeable by construction. The insights an ExpeL- or ReasoningBank-style distiller extracts from 400 random multi-hop QA episodes are overwhelmingly generic ('decompose the question, find the bridge entity, verify with a second search'), and B_a and B_b will therefore carry near-identical content. If so, Delta_info is near zero no matter whether substitution is real, and outcome (ii) 'complementarity' would be reported when the truth is 'the own/other contrast had no content difference to operate on.' Nothing in the design certifies otherwise: the procedural positive control B_a+proc10 certifies sensitivity to INSTANCE-specific value on 100 targeted S_test items, which is a different quantity from HALF-specific value; no preregistered statistic measures semantic divergence between B_a and B_b, and no crossover-specific positive control exists. The proposal's own numbers make this acute — with own-gain ~2pt and other-gain ~4.5pt the expected Delta_info is ~2.5pt against a stated MDE of 1.8-3.1pt and a claim threshold of 2pt, and any realistic degree of half-exchangeability pushes the true effect under the floor. Compounding this: the paper's title claim ('memory is just an un-optimized prompt') is carried by Prediction 4, a level equivalence at full data, which is only descriptive; and its TOST margins are wider than the effects being compared. 'I1_ab x C_ab within 4pt of I1_ab x M_ab' and 'I0 x C_a TOST-equivalent to I0 x M_a at +/-4pt' will pass even if compilation destroys the entire memory effect, since the field's bank effects on this model class are +0.6 to +3.6pt. As specified, the compile-once recommendation is close to unfalsifiable.
what_would_fix_it: (1) Split the two halves by task structure rather than at random — by question template / reasoning schema in E1, and by ALFWorld task type in E2 — so that B_a and B_b carry genuinely non-exchangeable procedural content and the own/other contrast has purchase. Random stratified halving actively destroys the signal the crossover is built to detect. (2) Preregister a bank-divergence measurement (item-level semantic overlap and cross-half retrieval rate: how often the top-7 items from B_a and B_b for the same test instance are paraphrases) and report it before unblinding; if the halves are exchangeable, Delta_info's null is uninformative and must be reported as such rather than as complementarity. (3) Add a positive control for the crossover contrast itself, not just for instance-specific value: seed each half with half-marked content of known usefulness and verify the crossover recovers it, exactly as proc10 does for the instance dimension. (4) Promote the level test — I1_ab x M_ab vs max(I1_ab x M0, I0 x M_ab) — to confirmatory and power it, since it, not Delta_info, is what the title asserts, and tighten the TOST margins from +/-4pt to something smaller than the memory effect being compared (e.g. +/-1.5pt), accepting that this costs n. (5) Define the iso-cost arm. (6) Reconsider G7's 4pt threshold: the proposal cites the field's own range as +0.6 to +3.6pt, so by its own literature it has preregistered a gate the modal world fails, and n=300 with SE~2.4pt makes the gate decision close to a coin flip in either direction.
missing_baseline: A compute-matched inference control: spend memory's injection budget on inference instead of on context. Memory injection at k=7 costs both tokens and prefill; a reviewer will demand that the no-memory agent be given the equivalent budget as extra tool calls (e.g. 11 rather than 8) or self-consistency at k=2-3 with majority vote, and will suspect that this alone recovers most of the +0.6 to +3.6pt bank gain. I3 does not cover this — padding I0 with task-generic boilerplate is a deliberately useless use of the budget and only bounds a length artifact, not a compute-reallocation rival. This matters most for the paper's efficiency recommendation ('the second container is cheaper to serve'), which is asserted but never measured against a cost-matched alternative. Notably, an 'iso-cost' arm appears twice in the submission — 4,400 episodes in the Tier 2 compute arithmetic, and first in the Tier 2 contingency cut order — but is defined nowhere: it has no artifact entry, no cell in the 25-row grid, no prediction, and no membership in any Holm family. Secondary omission: no truly out-of-distribution bank (items distilled from a different corpus or task) as a negative control for presence-of-retrieval effects; the shuffled-bank sanity check is mentioned only in passing in Ablations and never given a cell or an n.
preprint_collision: Well above the standard for this section, and it should be credited: a dated scan (2026-09-03, prior 2026-08-21), 15 named HuggingFace Papers queries over 244 papers, by-id verification for 54 arXiv IDs, committed scan records, an explicit two-channel rule for dropping a citation, a correction that reinstates five papers wrongly retracted in v2, and a withdrawal of the v2 novelty sentence in light of EvoAgentBench. That is a real search, not a gesture, and I found no preprint in my own knowledge that already runs an own-bank-vs-other-bank crossover at a fixed optimized instruction. Three concrete weaknesses remain. (a) The single most novelty-threatening paper, EvoAgentBench (2607.05202), was verified from a PDF supplied by the PI while arXiv is unreachable from the compute node — so every load-bearing absence claim ('no combined optimizer-plus-memory condition', 'the word token-matching does not occur', 'no paired test') rests on a source no reviewer can independently check, and a web snippet in the same submission is already documented as having misreported that paper's numbers (+7 vs the PDF's +3.6). If any of those absences is wrong, the contribution collapses to the crossover alone. (b) The proposal itself flags that the appendix of 2608.14036 has not been opened — appendices are precisely where a GEPA-plus-memory ablation would sit, and the residual-risk paragraph names that exact scenario. Flagging a hole is not closing it. (c) Coverage of the most dangerous window is thin: arXiv unreachable, Semantic Scholar rate-limited without a key, so the last two months are effectively HuggingFace-Papers-only (44 papers dated >= 2026-06), which is a popularity-biased sample and systematically misses the untrending preprint most likely to scoop a measurement paper. Net: the check is a strength of the submission, but the novelty argument is single-sourced at its most critical point.
